messages:
maria-cs: FYI received a high-severity from a paying customer (Acme Retail) — they see translations degrade after the weekend rollout. customer says French/Portuguese answers are now in English or overly formal. asked for triage.

jordan-support: Can you paste the customer repro and the API route they used? also which model & route did we promote? :eyes:

maria-cs: They upgraded to our hosted default after we flipped the rollout (global) to rwd-lingua-v2.2 at ~2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. Customer originally pinned rwd-lingua-v2.0. They didn't pin and got promoted. Repro below from customer (redacted keys):

```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "rwd-lingua-v2.2",
  "input": "Traduire en français: 'Our store hours are 9am-6pm, closed Sundays.'",
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "max_tokens": 80,
  "locale_hint": "fr-FR"
}
```

Customer response now (they sent these exact strings):

- Expected: "Nos horaires d'ouverture sont de 9h à 18h, fermé le dimanche."
- Got (v2.0.0): "Nos horaires d'ouverture sont de 9h à 18h, fermé le dimanche." ✅
- Got (v2.2 rollout): "Our store hours are 9am to 6pm. We are closed on Sundays." ❌ (English)

They also showed Portuguese prompts returning English or overly formal Brazilian Portuguese (tu vs você flip). They say it started immediately after the global rollout/canary promotion.

ingrid-ml: Thanks — do we have sampled logs for those customer requests? request_id or trace? Did they hit any fallback variant or a different region? If the request fell back to a compat model that could explain language mismatch.

maria-cs: Customer included request_id headers: `x-rwd-req: rwd-req-8f7c2b` and region us-east-1. They also attached a short trace (screenshot) showing `model_variant: rwd-lingua-v2.2` and `fallback_used: false`. Customer confirms no 5xx or 429 — responses returned fine but wrong language.

devon-ops: deploy-bot shows rollout graph — canary -> 20% -> 100% on 2026-03-14 02:07 UTC. No capacity issues. I pulled routing logs for that request id: all served by us-east-1 pool-3 on gpu-cluster-22. No fallback coded. No errors in proxy.

ingrid-ml: OK can we get a pair of full request/response tokens for a few samples? ideally with input + output strings and model metadata (sequence length, top_k). Also want to know if locale_hint is being honored in v2.2. I'm worried that a tokenizer change or locale detection heuristics regressed.

maria-cs: Sent two more examples from customer in DMs. Pasted one more here (customer redacted email):

```text
Prompt: "Translate to PT-BR: 'Return policy: 30 days with receipt.'"
v2.0 -> "Política de devolução: 30 dias com a nota fiscal."
v2.2 -> "Return policy: 30 days with receipt." (English)
Headers: x-rwd-req: rwd-req-8f9d11, model_variant: rwd-lingua-v2.2, region: eu-west-1
```

jordan-support: Are any customers hitting `language_detection` feature toggle? maybe v2.2 enabled an auto-detect pipeline that prefers English when uncertain. Can we check feature-flag history?

devon-ops: I checked FF service: `auto_locale_routing` was enabled globally for v2.2 canary on 2026-03-13 and promoted with the model. It should only change routing to locale-specific variants, not language switching. But logs show `detected_locale: en-US` for some requests that had `locale_hint: fr-FR`. Hmm.

ingrid-ml: That suggests detection model output changed — maybe the locale classifier was shipped as part of the v2.2 bundle and its calibration shifted. Need minimal repro we can run in staging. Can someone paste the exact HTTP request we can replay (without auth) and a stable prompt set.

maria-cs: Customer agreed to us replaying. I have 3 request_ids and timestamps. I'll drop them in #sec-ops DM with the signed POA. For public thread, they gave permission to repro but not to post logs. TL;DR: they want a rollback if we can't root cause quickly.

jordan-support: Prioritize — pinging @ingrid-ml and @devon-ops for an urgent rollback decision. If the classifier calibration broke production translations, rollback to rwd-lingua-v2.0 is reasonable while we debug. :exclamation:

devon-ops: We have automatic rollback window until 2026-03-15 05:00 UTC but that was already passed. Manual rollback possible; risk profile low (state-less model). I'll queue a manual promotion back to v2.0 for hosted default. Need approval from Product, but can do emergency revert if CS signals High impact.

ingrid-ml: I'll run quick A/B on staging comparing v2.0 vs v2.2 for the customer's prompts. If we can reproduce language flip locally then it's definitely model behavior. If not, we check locale-detection and routing. ETA 45m.

maria-cs: Customer impact: three enterprise customers reported similar behavior in APAC/EU (not just Acme). They call it a "language flip". Billing unaffected but product UX broken. They've requested rollback ASAP and a postmortem.

jordan-support: Noted. I'll coordinate with Sales/Account to indicate rollback plan if we confirm. Also capturing customer examples for evals.

devon-ops: Initiating rollback checklist: 1) Notify infra owners 2) Promote rwd-lingua-v2.0 to default 3) Monitor error/latency metrics 4) Inform customers. Need green light from product. tagging @product-lead (out of channel)

ingrid-ml: Quick note — can we also snapshot tokenizer vocab/merges between v2.0 and v2.2? If tokenization changed it could affect locale detection heuristics. I'll diff hash of tokenizer assets.

maria-cs: Customer asked for timeline; told them we'll revert if we see consistent repro. Keeping them updated. :pray:

deploy-bot: roll/graph: rwd-lingua-v2.2 promoted -> 100% at 2026-03-14T02:07:13Z. rollback available manual.

jordan-support: Thanks team. @ingrid-ml @devon-ops please update thread when you have repro or rollback decision. I'll keep CS loop open.

(THREAD END)
